## Definition

An **independent t-test** (also called unpaired or two-sample t-test) compares the means of two separate groups of participants. It tests whether the difference between group means is significantly different from zero.

## When to Use

Use an independent t-test when:

- Comparing two different groups of participants
- Groups are independent (no participant in both groups)
- Testing a between-groups design
- Data are approximately normally distributed (or n > 30 per group)

## The Formula

$$t = \frac{\bar{X}_1 - \bar{X}_2}{SE_{pooled}}$$

Where the pooled standard error depends on whether variances are assumed equal.

## Assumptions

| Assumption | Check |
|------------|-------|
| Independence | Participants only in one group |
| Normality | Data approximately normal in each group |
| Homogeneity of variance | Similar spread in both groups |
| Continuous data | Interval or ratio scale |

## Welch's t-test

When variances are unequal, use **Welch's t-test** (the default in R):

- Does not assume equal variances
- Adjusts degrees of freedom
- More robust in most situations

## Effect Size

Calculate **Cohen's d**:

$$d = \frac{\bar{X}_1 - \bar{X}_2}{s_{pooled}}$$

| d value | Interpretation |
|---------|----------------|
| 0.2 | Small effect |
| 0.5 | Medium effect |
| 0.8 | Large effect |

## R Code Example

```r
# Welch's t-test (default, does not assume equal variance)
t.test(score ~ group, data = mydata)

# Student's t-test (assumes equal variance)
t.test(score ~ group, data = mydata, var.equal = TRUE)

# Effect size
library(effectsize)
cohens_d(score ~ group, data = mydata)
```

## Reporting (APA Style)

> An independent-samples t-test showed that Group A (*M* = 72.3, *SD* = 8.4) scored significantly higher than Group B (*M* = 65.1, *SD* = 9.2), *t*(58) = 3.21, *p* = .002, *d* = 0.82.

## Non-Parametric Alternative

If assumptions are violated, use the [Mann-Whitney U Test](mann-whitney-u.qmd).

## DataLab Connection

The **[Mind Palace](../datalab/mindpalace.qmd)** station uses an independent t-test to compare memory recall between Lab 304A (abstract words, music) and Lab 304B (concrete words, silence). The two lab groups are independent — no participant is in both conditions.
